definition: Scheduled routine revision: an advance or preliminary estimate replaced by a revised one in the next regular release(s), including the routine concurrent re-estimation of seasonal factors that accompanies each release, and the BLS PPI recalculation about four months after first publication.
Annual (or periodic) revision benchmarking monthly estimates to annual surveys or the Economic Census, usually with historical corrections and updated seasonal adjustment models.
Annual recalculation of seasonal factors that revises several years of seasonally adjusted data without benchmarking (BLS CPI and PPI: with the January release).
Introduction of a new survey sample. May be linked so that no level shift is visible.
Change of index reference base, units, classification system (e.g. NAICS restatement) or population/coverage definition (e.g. employer-only).
Documented change in estimation methodology or weights that revises history (e.g. CPI expenditure-weight update with revision of seasonally adjusted indexes).
Model-based series whose full history is re-estimated at each release (e.g. BTS Transportation Services Index).
Agency-announced correction of erroneous published values.
Revision observed in the real-time record whose cause could not be established from agency sources. An honest final label.
Proposal-only state: no rule applies. Never allowed as a final label.
Not a drift event: new observations appended, no published value changed.
Not a drift event: ALFRED vintage holds a rolling window; the oldest observation drops out, nothing revised.
